summary: @servicetitan/design-system 14.5.10 executes obfuscated payload via downloaded Bun runtime on install
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall="node setup.mjs", which runs automatically on npm install. setup.mjs detects platform and architecture, downloads a Bun runtime binary from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases (v1.3.13) into a temporary directory, marks it executable, and then invokes it against a sibling file math_init.js at the tarball root. math_init.js is a 727KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle with hex-mangled identifiers and a rotating string-array cipher (WV8StW / n7gIxM), consistent with heavily obfuscated code designed to evade Node-based static inspection by executing under the freshly fetched alien runtime. The package advertises itself as a React/CSS design-system library and has no legitimate need for a Bun runtime or a `math_init.js` payload. Additionally, package.json declares `files: ["dist", "readme.md"]`, but setup.mjs (11KB) and math_init.js (727KB) are present at the tarball root without being listed in the manifest — the smuggled-artifact pattern consistent with a compromised publish inserting attacker files into an otherwise-legitimate package. The Bun-fetch destination is a legitimate project domain, but the payload it executes is package-local, obfuscated, unrelated to the package's declared purpose, and undeclared in the manifest — an alternate-runtime dropper that executes attacker-controlled code on the installer's machine at `npm install` time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
